references.context: Category theory: ordinary comma category of functors F:A→C, G:B→C, whose objects are triples (a,b,u:F(a)→G(b)) and morphisms are compatible commuting squares. Includes (j↓H) and (H↓j) with their opposite arrow directions as different instances; no assumption u is invertible.
references.matching_note: The ordinary comma-category construction specializes to one fixed source or target object; the arrow orientation remains explicit in the source and the existing iso-comma category is strictly more restrictive in requiring an isomorphism.

references.disposition: The oriented maps j→H(i) are precisely the objects defining the under-comma category (j↓H), whose construction already has an existing provisional prerequisite; no separate source-local arrow-object identity is needed. The arrow direction is essential and must not be reversed.
The comma category must be nonempty and connected at each j, not merely at some objects.
references.phrase: for every object j of J

references.context: Group theory: order of an element g in group G, the least positive integer n such that g^n=e_G when such n exists, otherwise infinite; here G=F^× and g=ζ.
references.reason: Element order in a multiplicative group is independently reusable, stronger than merely satisfying ζ^n=1 for some chosen exponent.
references.matching_note: Exact order n for a primitive n-th root differs from mere n-th-root status; preserve root-of-unity convention when characteristic divides n.

references.disposition: Exact order rules out proper divisor orders even though such elements also satisfy ζ^n=1.

irreducible closed subset Z of X
references.context: General topology: nonempty closed subset Z⊆X whose subspace topology is irreducible, equivalently Z cannot be expressed as union of two proper relatively closed subsets; Z need not be a maximal irreducible component.
references.reason: An irreducible closed subset combines reusable closedness in X and irreducibility of the induced topology, distinct from an irreducible component and from a generic point itself.
references.matching_note: Compare existing irreducible-space meaning.e0dd0b0cffcfff0b.irreducible-topological-space; nonempty and ambient-closed conditions must be retained.

references.disposition: The equality defines the generic-point property and is not a requirement that η be a unique point without sobriety.
